report: initial classifiers report (2026-10-22): an initial setup, sanity-checked on 15 recorded runs; cut-off 0.15 since 2026-10-23 (graph tune plan, unit A), a cost judgment, not a fit: a missed prior-art read costs a duplicate implementation, a wasted one a short read, and its reader writes no table rows, so no run can label it and it is never explored

asks_for_new_artifact.instructions: Read only the request, and its ticket when there is one. Does it ask for something new to exist, such as a new file, module, script, command, component, exported function or type, or a new kind of record, rather than only edits inside things that already exist?

criteria.true: The request asks for at least one new named thing to be created.
criteria.false: The request asks only for fixes, edits, renames, wording, or configuration changes inside things that already exist.

sits_beside_siblings.instructions: Read only the request, and its ticket when there is one. Is the new thing one more of a kind a program usually has several of, such as another command beside existing commands, another parser, check, handler, field, flag, or table row, so that code doing a similar job may already exist elsewhere in the repo?

criteria.true: The requested thing is another instance of a kind the codebase probably already has, or it needs a helper that likely exists already.
criteria.false: The request asks for no new thing, or for a thing unlike anything a codebase of this kind would already hold.

adds_capability.instructions: Read only the request, and its ticket when there is one. Does it add a new behavior or capability, something the program cannot do today, rather than fixing a defect, changing wording, removing code, or adjusting a value?

criteria.true: The request adds something the program cannot do today: a new behavior, command, option, field, or check.
criteria.false: The request only fixes a defect, changes wording or a value, removes code, or restructures what is already there.
